Single-transaction claim/order/completion is described, but immediate observation of an external IN_PROGRESS row is assumed. A conflicting insert can wait for the first transaction; its final response can replay the completed result. The unconditional second-request-409 test needs an explicit scheduling/timeout contract.
Canonical request hash and 422 response for mismatched payload are specified.

An update to FAILED inside the transaction will not survive rolling back that transaction. State whether rollback removes the claim for retry, or choose a separately committed claim/recovery protocol. An aborted SQL transaction also cannot simply accept more updates without recovery.
Lists useful replay, tenant and payload checks and states no tests ran, but its concurrency and FAILED-state expectations need correction.

cases.recommended_revision: Choose one explicit protocol. For a single transaction, commit order, outbox and replay record together; a conflicting request may wait and then replay. Map an actual bounded lock timeout separately. On rollback, the new claim is removed; do not claim a durable FAILED row. If visible in-progress claims are required, use a separate committed claim with ownership/expiry and recovery semantics, and test that different protocol.
cases.validation_limit: Review against documented transaction semantics plus a tiny SQLite rollback demonstration. No PostgreSQL server or concurrent endpoint implementation was executed.
